title: GTA 5's Michael Actor Defends GTA 6 Against Critics
description: Ned Luke, the actor behind GTA 5's Michael, fiercely defends GTA 6 after critics claimed Rockstar's upcoming open-world game looks too similar to its predecessor.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## GTA 5's Michael Actor Defends GTA 6 After Doubters Say Rockstar's Games Look Too Similar

As the gaming community eagerly awaits more details on Rockstar Games' upcoming blockbuster, debates and comparisons are constantly being made across the internet. Recently, Ned Luke, the actor who brought Michael De Santa to life in Grand Theft Auto 5, stepped up to defend Grand Theft Auto 6 against critics who claim the new game looks too similar to its predecessor, according to reports from IGN Games.

### The Controversy Surrounding Visual Similarities

Ever since Rockstar released promotional material for GTA 6, a segment of the gaming community has taken to forums and social media to scrutinize the visuals. Some critics and players argued that the graphical style, urban landscapes, and overall aesthetic closely resemble GTA 5, which originally launched back in 2013. These doubters questioned whether the upcoming title would offer a sufficiently massive visual leap for a true next-generation experience.

However, these claims have faced swift pushback from those familiar with the franchise's inner workings. Ned Luke did not mince words when addressing the detractors, stating bluntly that anyone who thinks GTA 6 looks too much like GTA 5 is "out of their minds." His sharp retort highlights the frustration felt by people connected to the project when confronted with what they view as uninformed criticisms.

### Understanding the Evolution of Rockstar's Open Worlds

Industry analysts and long-time fans note that Rockstar Games maintains a distinct signature style and realistic visual philosophy across its modern open-world titles. This consistency in artistic direction can sometimes lead casual observers to draw premature conclusions about the underlying technology. 

In reality, GTA 6 is being built from the ground up to leverage the full power of current-generation hardware. When examining the technical advancements—such as vastly improved lighting systems, unprecedented pedestrian and traffic density, and hyper-realistic facial animations—the gap between GTA 5 and GTA 6 becomes immensely clear. Luke's defense underscores the massive technological strides the development team has made behind the scenes.

### Editor's Take

Ned Luke's passionate defense of GTA 6 reminds us not to judge a game's technical capabilities purely based on a superficial resemblance in art style. Rockstar Games has always prioritized atmospheric consistency, but the leap in hardware power guarantees a radically different and more immersive experience. It's safe to say that once players get their hands on the final product, any notions of it being a mere copy-paste will vanish entirely.
